FEEDBACK: Repair the envelope logic to prevent an accidental pass: the current query allows a non-highest intended point to appear as an upper-waterline point whenever another upper point at the same longitudinal position covers the higher intended point. Require every upper profile point to equal, within tolerance, an intended profile point at the corresponding longitudinal position and require that no intended point at that position is higher; also require every intended longitudinal position to have such a maximal upper point. Constrain hasUpperIceWaterline to exactly one value and add maxCount 1 to each point coordinate and to each quantity's numericValue and unit so alternative values cannot satisfy the query selectively. Keep the ship target, canonical paths, decimal metre quantities, and tolerance-based comparisons.

Remove the invented relative/absolute tolerances. They can treat distinct longitudinal positions as identical and accept a UIWL below the actual highest intended waterline. Compare decimal longitudinal positions exactly, require every intended position to have an upper-waterline point, require every upper point to correspond to an intended point at that position, and require its vertical coordinate to equal the maximum intended vertical coordinate there (equivalently, match one intended value and reject any greater intended value). Retain the metre and xsd:decimal constraints.

Replace the mirrored, deeply nested EXISTS/FILTER NOT EXISTS cross-product with one bounded SPARQL aggregation constraint that computes MAX intended verticalCoordinate for each longitudinalPosition and verifies bidirectional equality of the upper-waterline profile: every intended position must have an upper point at that maximum, and every upper point must equal the computed maximum at an intended position. Retain the existing SHACL Core ownership, cardinality, datatype, and metre-unit constraints.
